read_this_first: THE CLAIM, IN THE CODING DOMAIN: let the system experience a fix once and it has learned it; so show it the best fixes and it repairs what comes next. QUIXBUGS_ONE_FIX_TRANSFER_20261111_V1 asked this of the tree's retention organ by itself. THIS MEASUREMENT asks it of the tree's repair SOLVER -- its search together with that memory, not edited, called with the arguments the tree's own campaign gives it -- on all 40 QuixBugs bugs (one defect each, written by other people; nothing else in this tree mentions them). RESULT. With nothing taught the solver repairs 5 of 40 (get_factors, knapsack, pascal, quicksort, sieve); every repair counted was confirmed by asking the bug's own tests again after the solver was done. THE SAME BUG AGAIN: the 4 repairs that left a lesson were all repeated from memory on a fresh copy of the bug with no search, in 1.9 s and 3 processes each, where the search had taken 5.5 to 228.6 s and 18 to 1035 processes (the fifth repair, sieve, left no lesson: the organ refused it). THE OTHER FIXES TAUGHT FIRST: with the published fixes of all the other bugs offered as lessons (the organ accepted 22 of the 40), memory proposed a repair for 3 of the 40 bugs and all 3 were repaired without a search; 2 of them the solver repairs anyway, so the lessons added 1 bug (gcd): 6 of 40. Where memory proposed nothing the solver searched as it does with an empty memory (3 such bugs run in full: same outcome, processes started within 2 of each other). WHAT THE SOLVER DID NOT DO: 31 searches ended by themselves with no repair (27 after 45 to 245 s; 4 that had not ended at this measurement's limit of 300 s were run again alone and ended with no repair after 330 to 642 s); 3 bugs it would not start on because the buggy program never ends (bitcount, find_first_in_sorted, sqrt); on 1 (levenshtein) it raised an error of its own and stopped, both times it was run. A PILOT, NOT A RESULT: the solver's own bound on how many single changes it keeps per file, raised from its default 24 to its ceiling 128, on 6 of the unrepaired bugs: 1 of 6 repaired (next_permutation, in 12 s, run twice), the other 5 unchanged. FOR SCALE, published elsewhere and not reproduced here: language models repair 31 to 40 of these 40 bugs. WHAT THIS SAYS: remembering a repair is real here, exact and cheap, and what is remembered is that repair. What repairs a bug nobody has shown it is the search; the search finds 5 of 40, and 39 demonstrations of other repairs moved that to 6. Zero model calls, zero spend, no capability credit claimed. One run; nobody else has re-run it.

the_repairs_read_one_by_one.note: read by the producer; 'repaired' in the counts means only that the solver said so, the file changed and the bug's own tests pass when asked again
the_repairs_read_one_by_one.knapsack: the published fix (weight < j becomes weight <= j)
the_repairs_read_one_by_one.pascal: the published fix (range(0, r) becomes range(0, r + 1))
the_repairs_read_one_by_one.sieve: the published change (any becomes all) written with one more pair of brackets, which is why is_the_published_fix says false
the_repairs_read_one_by_one.quicksort: another change with the same effect: the published fix lets elements equal to the pivot into 'greater' (x >= pivot), this one lets them into 'lesser' (x <= pivot)
the_repairs_read_one_by_one.get_factors: another change: the loop runs up to n instead of up to its square root, so n itself is found as a factor. The factors come out right; the program is slower than with the published fix, which returns [n] at the end
the_repairs_read_one_by_one.gcd__the_one_bug_the_lessons_added: def gcd(a, b) becomes def gcd(b, a): the two parameters change places, which turns the faulty recursion into Euclid's algorithm with the roles exchanged. Right in effect; not the published fix (gcd(b, a % b)). The earlier measurement shows which lesson it comes from: shortest_path_lengths

the_five_runs_that_did_not_end_in_the_ma.why: in the main run four solver runs were stopped at this measurement's wall limit of 300 s and one ended with an error; a stopped run is not the solver's own answer, so the five were run again by themselves with a limit of 2400 s (same code, two at a time)
the_five_runs_that_did_not_end_in_the_ma.record: copied from the run's own log lines as the producer read them; the result file of this side run was on the machine's scratch disk and was lost when the machine was reset before it was committed
the_five_runs_that_did_not_end_in_the_ma.so: none of the five is a repair; the counts stand; the four stopped runs are searches that end with no repair when given the time

what_the_published_fixes_of_the_35_unrep.note: the producer's reading of the 35 published fixes, each bug in one group; it says what kind of change the missing repair is, not why the search missed it

with_128_the_first_time.record: copied from the run's own log lines as the producer read them; the result file of this side run was on the machine's scratch disk and was lost when the machine was reset before it was committed

next_permutation.the_repair: if perm[j] < perm[i] becomes if not perm[j] < perm[i]. The published fix is perm[i] < perm[j]; the two differ only when the two elements are equal

the_other_five.record: copied from the run's own log lines as the producer read them; the result file of this side run was on the machine's scratch disk and was lost when the machine was reset before it was committed

skills_given_to_agents_2026.says: SkillsBench, 84 tasks, 7 agent-model pairs: skills written by people raise the pass rate by 16.2 points on average (4.5 in software engineering); skills the model writes for itself change it by -1.3
skills extracted by models from their own experience help on average and lower the score in 25% of extractor-target pairings
CODESKILL: a skill bank managed by a policy that was itself trained raises the average pass rate by 9.69 points over no skills

checks_of_the_tests.tests: 61 for this tool (canonical/tests/test_quixbugs_repair_solver_v1.py): 47 put a stand-in where the solver's process, the organ and the tests go and pin which bug is given to the solver with which store, what counts as repaired (the solver's word, a changed file and the bug's tests asked again -- all three), what counts as coming from memory, and how it is added up; 7 run real processes around a stand-in worker (stopped at the wall limit with everything it started, an answer after other output, a worker that dies, the tree it runs in); 7 run the real solver with the real organ on three small programs written for the tests

seeded_faults_in_the_tool.how: every place in the tool where a comparison, a boolean, a number, a short string or a one-line statement could be changed was changed, one at a time, and the tests were run: the stand-in tests for the measurement and the summary, the process tests for the process wrapper, and for the places only a real store can show, the real-solver tests
seeded_faults_in_the_tool.what_is_left: making a directory that the next call makes anyway (4); collecting a process after it was killed (1); the decimals of a time (1); a text-comparison option that does nothing on short texts (1); one worker or one item going through the pool instead of the plain loop, with the same outcome and the same number of runs at a time (3); what a missing time counts as (4); the command line's help text, flushing, printing of the summary, the layout of the output file and the main guard (9). None changes a reported count
seeded_faults_in_the_tool.record: the counts are as the producer read them from the fault runs; the script and its result files were scratch and were lost in the reset. The assertions they led to are in the test file

leaks_that_were_looked_for: the answer: each bug was laid out for the solver as the buggy program, its tests and their data and nothing else; none of the 90 projects laid out in the run held the correct programs (looked at on disk before the reset), and a test holds that no file the solver is given contains the repairing line

the bug's own lesson: with the other fixes taught first, each bug was offered 21 lessons if its own fix had been stored and 22 otherwise, its own never among them (asserted on this record when it was written; a test holds it)
the rules the tree ships with: every store used here starts empty (seed off), as in the earlier measurement

a repair that is only the solver's word: all 12 runs in which the solver said it had repaired also passed when the bug's tests were asked again by a fresh oracle on the file left on disk (asserted on this record when it was written)

limits: one run. Where the search was run twice it repeated itself: the three check bugs started 543/544, 465/466 and 853/855 processes with and without lessons and ended the same way; knapsack, quicksort and gcd had ended the same way in a trial of the tool before the full run. The tool was not changed between that trial and the run
two solver runs side by side on a two-processor machine: the seconds are not clean timings. Outcomes depend on time only through the 8 s limit for one run of a bug's tests and through the wall limit
the 8 s limit for one run of a bug's tests is this measurement's choice. The error on levenshtein is the solver's tracer running out of that limit; a longer limit was not tried
the solver was called with its default bounds, as the tree's own campaign calls it; the pilot shows that one of them matters for one bug

the lessons are the published fixes, i.e. the best demonstrations there are; the organ refused to store 18 of the 40 (14 FAILED_MUTATED_TWIN_VERIFICATION, 3 TRAINING_BASELINE_DID_NOT_EXECUTE_FAILING_TESTS, 1 NON_GENERALIZABLE_SNIPPET), so each bug was offered 21 or 22 lessons, never its own
